Missouri Meerschaum Corncob Pipe Lot
2 Piece Set, Vintage Tobacco Smoking Pipes
Corncob, Wood, and Plastic, Approximately 6 Inches Long
A pair of vintage corncob tobacco pipes manufactured by the Missouri Meerschaum Company of Washington, Missouri. Founded in 1869, Missouri Meerschaum is the world's oldest and largest manufacturer of corncob pipes, known for their cool-smoking properties and historical significance in American culture. These two examples feature different bowl textures and stem designs, ideal for collectors or enthusiasts of traditional smoking implements.
Lot includes two distinct corncob pipes with wooden stems and amber-toned mouthpieces

Handcrafted construction utilizing natural corncob for a unique porous smoking experience
Sizes range from approximately 5.5 to 5.75 inches in total length
Condition:
Bowls show evidence of previous use with light charring visible inside the chambers. The exterior of the corncob bowls remains structurally sound with natural variations in texture. Wood stems are secure. Plastic mouthpieces are intact without significant bite marks or cracks. Base label on one pipe is present and legible with minor edge wear. Generally well-preserved vintage condition.

Buy confidently, knowing this is an authentic vintage piece, ideal for gifting or personal enjoyment.

description:
Rock and Mineral Collection
Educational Specimen Lot With Labeled Display Board
Approximately 68 Pieces, Natural and Tumbled Stones
A comprehensive geological collection featuring a wide array of rock and mineral specimens. This lot includes a primary identification board housing 48 distinct samples, each labeled for easy study, alongside a secondary assortment of loose tumbled and raw stones. The collection provides a broad survey of mineralogy, including various silicates, oxides, and carbonates.
Identification board with 48 specimens including Pyrite, Amethyst, and Turquoise
Approximately 20 additional loose stones including a large raw Rose Quartz piece
Specimens range from raw crusts to polished tumbled pebbles
Identification board remains sealed in original protective plastic wrap

description:

This lot contains a variety of rocks, minerals, and fossils including a multicolored stone marked 'Lee Spiller', a white quartz or calcite geode, clear quartz crystal, agate geodes, chalcedony, quartz clusters, an ammonite fossil, and a trilobite fossil.

The specimens vary in size and form a diverse collection of geological and paleontological samples.

description:
Mineral Specimen Collection - Mixed Lot
Quartz, Calcite, and Various Natural Stones
Natural Geological Specimens
This collection features a variety of natural geological specimens, anchored by a significant large white geode with a visible crystalline interior. These pieces offer a range of textures, from raw, jagged mineral clusters to smooth tumbled accent stones, making them ideal for display, geological study, or as a foundational set for a mineral collection. The diverse array of colors and formations provides a comprehensive look at common mineral structures including druzy quartz and calcite cleavage planes.
Pieces Included:
Large white quartz geode, approximately 6.5 inches tall with hollow crystalline center
Medium raw mineral specimens (2) featuring layered crystal structures and earthy inclusions
Yellow raw and tumbled stones (4) with vibrant saturation
Green tumbled stone (1) with semi-translucent appearance
Clear and smoky mineral accent pieces (multiple) in various sizes
White flat mineral slab (1) with matte finish
Condition:
Natural geological specimens in raw and tumbled states. The large geode is intact as a specimen half with well-defined internal crystals. Smaller pieces show typical natural variations, inclusions, and fractures inherent to mineral formations. No significant modern damage beyond natural extraction characteristics. Total collection weight is 5.14 pounds.
